chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Sunnah cannot be analogized. Do you not see that a woman makes up her fasts but does not make up her prayers?
O Aban! The Sunnah, when analogized, obliterates the Religion.

key_terms.السُّنَّةَ: Sunnah — the normative practice of the Prophet (SAWW) and the Imams (AS), which must be received and followed as transmitted, without subjection to human analogical derivation
key_terms.تُقَاسُ: is analogized — subjected to qiyas, the method of deriving rulings by logical analogy contested between Sunni and Shia jurisprudential traditions
key_terms.مُحِقَ: is obliterated/annihilated — the Religion is eradicated when human reasoning overrides divinely revealed and transmitted rulings

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declare that the Sunnah cannot be analogized, and what example does he use in this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) categorically rejects the use of qiyas (analogical reasoning) in religious law, addressing his trusted companion Aban ibn Taghlub directly. He cites the established ruling that a menstruating woman must make up missed fasts but is entirely exempt from making up missed prayers — a ruling utterly inexplicable by human analogy — to demonstrate that the Sunnah operates on divinely ordained logic that transcends human derivation. He concludes with a stern warning: applying qiyas to the Sunnah does not merely distort religion, it obliterates it.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, from Aban Bin Taghlub, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Sunnah cannot be analogized. Can you not see that the woman fulfils her Fasts but she does not fulfil her Salat?
O Aban! The Sunnah, when analogised, obliterates (demolishes) the Religion’.
en.sarwar: 15. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan Yahya from ’Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Aban ibn Taghlib from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“The Sunnah, tradition of the holy Prophet (s.a.) can not be leaned through analogy. Consider a woman has to make up for her fast missed due to menses but she does not have to make up for the prayers that she would miss in such times.
O Aban, the use of analogy destroys religion.”
